messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME (acct acme-inc) opened a severity-2 ticket — p99 tail latency jumped from ~190ms to ~1.5s starting ~2026-03-15 08:40 UTC. They see sporadic 502s and some requests that never finish. Linked graphs: https://grafana/redwood/acme-p99
acme_cse: seeing this on our end too — a bunch of requests stalled, then a few returned 502 with "backend unavailable". No code changes on our side. Payloads are long (avg seq_len ~900 tokens), concurrency ~18. We only saw problems after the 08:30 deploy.
devon_oncall: can you paste the model + instance info? any rate-limit/burst changes? Also allocate the runtime logs for the timeframe.
maria_support: Model: redwood/open-medium-quant (int8-ish runtime path). Dedicated pool: gpu-a100-40gb, autoscale off, reserved 6 gpus for ACME. Batch config: max_batch=16, prefer_latency=false. Attached log excerpt (trunc):
```
[08:41:12] request id=rcp-993 path=/v1/completions seq_len=912 batch_id=345 queue_wait_ms=12
[08:41:12] allocate kv_cache=42MB -> 1.1GB (growth +26%) alloc_attempt=1
[08:41:12] slab_alloc failed: need=482MB free=210MB - falling back to slow path
[08:41:12] OOM-handler: reclaiming slabs... evict_candidates=0
[08:41:13] p99_token_latency jump to 1.2s
[08:41:14] 502 returned to client id=rcp-995
```
sam_sre: logs show repeated slab_alloc failures and "evict_candidates=0" which usually means KV/batch growth is starving slab free lists — looks like fragmentation + unbounded KV growth for long sequences. Also check nvidia-smi for persistent allocation vs process free.
jia_runtime: can you run quick diagnostics on one affected host and paste output? two quick commands:
```
# GPU memory + processes
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
# runtime allocator stats (local debug endpoint)
curl -s http://localhost:8002/debug/allocator | jq . | sed -n '1,120p'
```
maria_support: got the outputs from host gpu-23:
```
GPU 0, NVIDIA A100, 38847 MiB / 40960 MiB
process: redwood-runtime pid=4123 mem=37.8GiB
allocator.stats: total_slabs=184 free_slabs=4 active_slabs=180 slab_fragmentation=0.82 kv_cache_bytes=28G
```
devon_oncall: kv_cache_bytes=28G on a 40G card + only 4 free slabs = bad. That explains the slow path and occasional OOMs. Two immediate suspects: (1) customer workload with long seq + large caching (KV growth), (2) allocator fragmentation leaving too few contiguous chunks.
acme_cse: can we temporarily reduce batch size? We can also route some traffic to a different pool if needed.
jia_runtime: short-term mitigations we should try (do one at a time):
- reduce max_batch to 4 for ACME route
- enable aggressive KV eviction for tenant (config key: runtime.kv.eviction=aggressive-ttl=10s)
- enable slab compaction pass (flag: runtime.allocator.compact=true) and roll hosts one-by-one
- if still bad, failover ACME to CPU fallback pool for short window
sam_sre: agree. Also recommend a rolling restart of one GPU host with slab compaction on to reclaim fragmentation rather than mass restart. Avoid restarting all hosts at once or we'll spike p50 for everyone.
maria_support: I'll request ACME permission to run mitigations. They approved reducing batch size and enabling eviction. Applying now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: config update for tenant=acme-inc max_batch=4 runtime.kv.eviction=aggressive-ttl=10s by maria_support at 2026-03-15T08:56:01Z
maria_support: changes applied to routing + tenant config. Monitoring.
(3m later)
maria_support: immediate improvement: p99 dropped to ~240ms, no new 502s. GPU mem usage down ~7GB on hosts serving ACME. Good sign.
devon_oncall: follow-ups and next steps:
- short-term: keep the aggressive eviction + batch=4 for 24h. Add an alert to warn if kv_cache_bytes > 20G on any host.
- mid-term: patch runtime allocator to run periodic compaction more aggressively when free_slabs < 8 (PR planned).
- long-term: add tenant-level protections (max_kv_cache_bytes, auto-burst-throttle) and improve routing to prefer lower-long-seq hosts.
sam_sre: also collect repro load: maria, can you provide the curl script ACME used so RnD can reproduce locally? We need exact concurrency and seq length distribution.
maria_support: ACME provided repro (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..18}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
    -d '{"model":"open-medium-quant","input": "<~900 token prompt>", "max_tokens":200}' &
done
wait
```
jia_runtime: created issue RNDR-1189 with initial analysis and assigned to runtime team. PR for allocator compaction heuristics targeting 2-day turnaround.
acme_cse: thanks team, customer is happy with mitigation. They asked for recommendations to avoid recurrence: we advised them to avoid very long single requests when possible, or use streaming + chunking; also offered a capacity increase quote if they want guaranteed headroom for long-seq workloads.
maria_support: marking this thread resolved from support side. Will keep monitor for 24h. :thumbsup:
devon_oncall: adding follow-up checklist to the incident runbook: 1) tenant batch cap; 2) kv eviction knob; 3) rolling compaction plan; 4) telemetry alert (kv_cache_bytes per host). I'll schedule a retro with eng-runtime tomorrow.
sam_sre: noted. closing loop after 24h, thanks Everyone. :white_check_mark:
